events.title: Guyana’s Brazil-frontier COVID travel restriction with weekly goods exceptions, 2020–2021
events.scope: Guyanese restriction on ordinary cross-border land travel at Lethem/Bonfim, with controlled essential exchanges
events.direction: Guyana-administered cross-border travel; entry from Brazil is directly documented.
events.movement: Ordinary travellers and cross-border trading communities; essential supplies were handled through exceptions.
events.exceptions: Thursday goods and limited shopping exchanges; October relaxation added Friday personal travel subject to health conditions.
events.imposing_authority: Government of Guyana and regional border/health authorities
events.enforcement: Official crossing restrictions and requested river patrols; informal river crossings were reported.
events.consequences: Local businesses reported hardship; October relaxation followed pressure from regional leaders and traders.
events.relationship: Resolves lead AM-L02. Distinct imposing authority from Brazil’s AM019; excludes Guyana–Suriname ferry AM034. Later weekday/daily extensions are phases, not new events.
events.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
events.official_rationale: Limit transmission of COVID-19 across the Brazil frontier.
events.context: Guyanese measures followed Brazil’s own entry restriction; these are separate decisions on the same frontier.
events.uncertainty: Guyanese start day not resolved; Brazil’s March 19 date is not copied. October 1 is a limited personal-travel relaxation, not full reopening. Reports vary on vaccination/PCR formulation and Friday hours, which are not asserted exactly. Stabroek’s retrospective 19 May 2020 onset conflicts with the official 27 March statement that travel was already suspended; it is not used to date onset.

events.title: Ecuador’s selected land-crossing security closures, December 2025–July 2026 partial reopening
events.scope: Ecuadorian restriction regime closing or limiting authorized land crossings except Rumichaca and Huaquillas; crossing-specific exceptions and reopenings
events.crossings: San Miguel; Macará–La Tina; Lalamor; Jimbura; La Balsa
events.direction: Entry and exit through affected Ecuadorian crossings; Colombian merchandise entry specifically documented in diplomatic record.
events.movement: Ordinary travellers, international buses and freight using affected secondary crossings.
events.exceptions: Rumichaca/Huaquillas remained authorized. San Miguel allowed controlled crude-oil movements and special permits. Macará retained some local work, study and medical access until a July 1 tightening.
events.imposing_authority: Government of Ecuador, border agencies and armed forces
events.enforcement: Military controls and closed migration/customs offices; informal river travel continued near San Miguel.
events.consequences: Loja–Piura bus service suspended; San Miguel users shifted to informal boats; local mobility and commerce affected.
events.relationship: Distinct from 2025 election restrictions AM042/AM049. One national policy family; southern phases are not counted as extra events.
events.status_observation: Status limited to dated evidence; no claim of present closure.
events.official_rationale: National security and control of illicit cross-border activity; southern reopening announcement specifically cites arms trafficking.
events.context: National concentration of formal passage at two gateways; subsequent exemptions and southern relaxation make this a phased restriction regime.
events.uncertainty: July 7 endpoint is Macará’s observed vehicle/pedestrian reopening, not full restoration of all named crossings. July 1 last-closed observation concerns Macará only. Uniform daily implementation at every crossing and the final nationwide endpoint are not established.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Regime from December 24, 2025 to the July 7, 2026 Macará partial reopening. No all-traffic duration computed.
